Hi Aisha,

Quick note ahead of the renewal: I understand Orion is evaluating a replatform with another vendor and they’ve submitted a pricing/throughput proposal that looks attractive on face value. Before you make any decisions, I want to propose a short benchmarking window and a concrete commercial path that keeps Orion on Redwood while addressing the capacity and price concerns.

Proposed immediate steps:
- Run a targeted throughput benchmark (we can mirror the competitor test you shared) — 48–72 hours.
- If the benchmarks show parity (or near-parity) on latency/throughput, we’ll offer a temporary committed capacity uplift + a one-time credit to offset migration evaluation costs.
- If you need a stronger contractual guarantee, we’ll provide a p95 latency SLO for the upgrade period and a rollback/fallback escalation path.

Can you share the competitor’s throughput test script (or the logs) and the target qps / input sequence distribution? I’ll loop in Monica (CS lead) and Neha (security/compliance) so we can scope the run.

Thanks,

Priyom,

Appreciate the quick outreach. Yes — we’ve received an aggressive commercial from CloudForge (their dedicated offering + onboarding credits). The exec team has asked for: 2x current throughput during peak, commitment for 12 months, and a clear migration cost offset.

We can share the test harness. High level: 95th percentile latency target currently is 150ms, traffic mix is 70% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 30% long (512–1024 tokens). Peak QPS target for the upgrade is ~1,200 qps sustained for a 30-minute window.

Two asks from our side if Redwood wants to be considered:
1) A short (3–7 day) benchmark showing p95 and end-to-end failure rate under the specified load.
2) A written term sheet with: pricing for the 12-month commitment, temporary credits for evaluation/migration, and a draft SLO.

I’ll send the test harness and logs in a separate email to make sure you have the right inputs. Procurement copied.

Best,

Folks — forwarding Orion’s ask. Short summary: they have a competitor offer on the table. They want a 3–7 day benchmark demonstrating 1,200 qps sustained with target p95 <= 150ms (their current bar).

What I need from CS + SRE:
- Can we run a like-for-like harness (I’ll attach their test script when it arrives). Prefer a focused 48–72 hour run to start.
- If we show parity or a clear path to parity, I want to propose this commercial package:
  * 12-month committed tranche for uplifted capacity (50% discount on uplift for the first 3 months while they validate)
  * One-time migration credit equal to 2 months of uplifted spend (applied over next invoice)
  * Explicit p95 latency SLO of 120ms for the committed configuration (with credit-backed remediation steps)
  * Dedicated onboarding support (3 weeks of white-glove CS assistance)

This is aggressive but still within our flexible concession band if the benchmark proves out. Please run the initial test and capture token-level costs, p95 latency, error rates, and recommended config (quantization, batch sizes, autoscale headroom).

Attachments: benchmark_run_instructions.md (internal runbook)

Thanks — Priyom

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Priyom — ran an initial 48-hour window mirroring Orion’s harness. Summary below, full report attached.

Highlights (48h run):
- Sustained peak: 1,250 qps for 35-minute windows (we exceeded target briefly to validate headroom).
- p95 latency (committed config): 118ms
- Error rate (5xx): 0.12% under peak
- Token-level cost: ~14% lower than the competitor estimate in their submission when normalized for token mix

Recommendations:
- Offer Orion a 12-month commit with the following commercial terms (draft):
  1) Uplifted capacity priced at $X per token (see attached proposed_terms_v3.docx)
  2) 50% discount on uplift for first 3 months to cover migration validation
  3) One-time migration credit equal to 2 months of uplift spend
  4) p95 latency SLO of 120ms for the committed config with a 15% service credit if missed >2 months in a row
  5) Dedicated onboarding (3-week runbook + two SRE on-call rotations during cutover)

I attached benchmark_report_v2.pdf with raw metrics, test parameters, and configuration notes (model variant, batch sizes, kernel choices). We also captured recommended quantization profile that keeps latency low while reducing cost.

If you want, I can prepare a short one-pager showing the normalized cost/latency comparison vs CloudForge for the execs.

— Monica

Aisha — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sending the harness. Monica’s team completed a mirrored run and we have a clear set of outcomes and a formal proposal attached. Key points below (see attached proposed_terms_v3.docx and SOW_orion_upgrade.pdf):

Executive summary:
- Performance: we met your target (p95 118ms on committed config) and sustained >1,200 qps; error profile under load is within acceptable bounds.
- Economics: normalized token cost is ~14% lower than the competitor’s estimate for the same workload after applying recommended quantization and batching.

Commercial offer (high level):
1) 12-month committed uplift for peak capacity (details in attached term sheet)
2) 50% discount on uplifted capacity for months 1–3 while you validate migration
3) One-time migration credit equal to 2 months of uplifted spend (applied to invoices)
4) p95 latency SLO of 120ms for committed config; 15% service credit if SLO missed for >2 months consecutively
5) Dedicated onboarding: 3 weeks of white-glove CS + two SRE rotations during cutover

Next steps:
- If this aligns, confirm by EOD Tue (05 Oct) and we’ll issue a DocuSign for the proposed terms (link included). Once signed we’ll schedule the production cutover run and reserve dedicated capacity.
- If you want tweaks (term length, credit schedule), tell us which items to prioritize and we’ll iterate quickly.

Quoted from your earlier note for context:
> "95th percentile latency target currently is 150ms... Peak QPS target for the upgrade is ~1,200 qps sustained for a 30-minute window."

Attachments: proposed_terms_v3.docx, SOW_orion_upgrade.pdf
